review.scope: Follow-up audit closure/ruling/malformed findings fixes to rejected b80ef055 review, plus new private stderr capture across ledger/publication/provenance transport. Source-only; no hosted verification or activation claimed. Preserve open original exit-128 cause and all gates.
findings: VERIFIED: Closure defect fixed. require_parent_closure checks every parent of each additional commit (rev-list --parents) against additions plus the pinned {BASE, SOURCE, original} boundary, so no unscanned side history between SOURCE and the ruling. Additions must be unique 40-hex non-original descendants of SOURCE and must include TRUST; original range pinned to exactly 82 commits.

VERIFIED: Ruling binding fixed. pinned_policy binds policy blob and evidence/decisions.md bytes by SHA-256 and additionally requires rev-parse TRUST^ == SOURCE (RULING_PARENT_MISMATCH), anchoring the ruling to its exact reviewed commit rather than a working-tree file.

VERIFIED: Malformed-findings defect fixed with privacy preserved. scan_commits passes policy error text through only when it full-matches [A-Z_]+; UnicodeError maps to NON_UTF8_PUBLICATION and all other caught exceptions to MALFORMED_PUBLICATION_STRUCTURE. Findings carry path_sha256/byte hashes, never path text, rejected content, or subprocess output; tests assert redaction for both rejection and malformed-policy paths.

VERIFIED: private_git transport is fail-closed and opaque. Stderr goes to per-invocation 0600 files in a uid-owned 0700 non-symlink directory refused if inside a Git checkout, with refusal before execution (test confirms empty directory). Exceptions expose only exit status/timeout plus the receipt directory name (from None suppresses chaining); result.stderr is scrubbed; stdout/stderr/shell overrides rejected; timeout preserves pre-kill bytes with fsync; receipts record argv_sha256 and stderr_sha256, never arguments, input, or content. Ledger, publication (including create), and provenance retrieval all route through it.

VERIFIED: Authority and gates preserved. publish/create require byte-exact externally supplied authority dicts; create demands exact field set, absent-ref lease, porcelain '*' status, and post-push ls-remote re-verification; checkpoint remains pinned to the pilot destination; limiter requires RATIFIED + OPERATOR_AUTHORIZED (+OPERATOR_AUTHORIZED_V1 for server admission), halts latch across midnight, reset/initialize remain operator-approval routes, and PROPOSED config short-circuits inactive. Docs claim no hosted verification, no activation, and leave the original exit-128 transport finding OPEN with no root cause assigned, matching scope.

SUGGESTION: scan_commits records metadata findings as raw str(error) from policy.scan_commit without the [A-Z_]+ code filter applied to blob findings, and a non-ValueError there would abort the whole audit instead of being recorded. Harmless with the hash-pinned policy (only the fixed COMMIT_METADATA_REJECTED code is raised) but asymmetric hardening; apply the same filter/mapping.

SUGGESTION: private_git.run accepts and silently ignores capture_output, which git_publication, dispatch_limiter, and fetch_provenance all pass. Behavior is a compatible superset (stdout always piped, stderr always private), but explicitly rejecting or documenting the kwarg would prevent misreading.

SUGGESTION: Receipt directories accumulate one per Git invocation with no bound or rotation (a single admission can spawn a dozen under CAS retries). A full diagnostics filesystem makes open('xb')/mkdtemp fail and all Git transport refuse — fail-closed but a self-inflicted availability risk; bound or rotate before hosted use, consistent with the doc's retention caveat.

SUGGESTION: scripts/pr5_retrospective_audit.py's own git() helper still uses raw subprocess.check_output(stderr=PIPE) rather than the private transport. CalledProcessError.__str__ omits stderr so printed output does not leak, but the captured stderr rides on the exception object — inconsistent with the new transport for an operator-run script.

NOTE: Shell/file tools were disabled in this session; the working tree could not be independently confirmed against 1b4d55b2. Review binds to the supplied source bytes. No tests were executed; all verification is source-only reading.
